yfs.a_date_sous: What is already sold, against the same lead time last year
yfs.a_date_expl_1: **Y-1 is rebuilt, never observed** — on every row, which is why the column does not repeat it. A booking sold before that date and cancelled since has disappeared from the comparison portfolio: Y-1 is underestimated, so the growth shown is flattering.
yfs.a_date_expl_2: **“Closed to sale” is not “nothing sold”.** A closed calendar explains a zero: it is not a commercial failure, it is a decision.
yfs.reference_sous_court: What is normal for this property
yfs.reference_sous: Median price by period type, over {ans} years
yfs.ref_expl_mediane: **Median, not average.** A discounted night does not move the median.
yfs.ref_expl_seuil: **Threshold: {nuits} nights and {resas} bookings.** Below that, the reference stays silent: a median computed on so few nights is an accident, not a norm. (Both thresholds come from the engine — they are not copied anywhere.)
yfs.ref_expl_longs: **{n} night(s) of long stays** set aside: a sliding rate over four weeks would make the norm instead of measuring it.
yfs.ref_expl_sans_prix: **{n} night(s) with no known price** left out of the calculation.
yfs.rythme_sous: Share of sales already made, so many days before the night
yfs.rythme_expl_1: **This is not an occupancy rate.** It is the share of final sales already made at that lead time: “36% at 30 days” means a third of what will sell was sold a month before.
yfs.rythme_expl_2: **Only reliable sale dates count.** A date recreated during a migration would put every sale on the same day and flatten the curve.
yfs.rythme_expl_3: A segment under the threshold shows no curve: a pace computed on a few nights is an anecdote.
yfs.projection_vide: Nothing to project in this window.
yfs.proj_expl_1: **“Share already sold” is a share of final sales, not an occupancy rate.** The expected total is extrapolated from what is already sold — capacity is never multiplied.
yfs.proj_expl_2: **Ahead or behind is measured against last year’s occupancy.** Without it, the engine would rather say nothing than invent a norm.
yfs.proj_expl_3: **It is a range, not a forecast.** The bold figure assumes the period will sell at its segment’s usual pace; the bounds come from the two curve steps around today’s lead time. Between 14 and 30 days before the night, this pace varies a lot — the range says so rather than hiding it.
yfs.proj_expl_4: **No projection on a closed period**: it would invent a shortfall that does not exist.
yfs.evenements_sous: School holidays, public holidays and long weekends
yfs.ev_scolaire_absent: The school calendar is not loaded: no holiday period is known. Every day counts as “outside holidays”, and the seasonal reference is skewed over the whole window.
yfs.ev_horizon: The official school calendar stops on **{date}**. Beyond it, holidays are not known: those days count as “outside holidays”, and the reference of the periods concerned is skewed. It must be reimported before that date.
yfs.ev_expl_1: **Other zones’ holidays count too** — a property hosts holidaymakers from all over France. But they are not worth yours: on this property, they bring the same price as a period outside holidays.
yfs.ev_expl_2: These dates are **read-only**: they come from the official calendar and the public holiday calculation, nothing here changes them.
yfs.exc_lecture_seule: You can view these periods, not change them: declaring an exception changes what the engine considers normal, and so the prices it will suggest.
yfs.exc_aucune: No period declared. Exceptional months — works, personal closure — therefore count as normal months in the reference.
yfs.exceptions_sous: What must not count as normal
yfs.exc_expl_1: **Since {date}.** The reference is computed over {ans} years: a period declared before that date would be saved without changing anything, and would not appear in this list.
yfs.exc_expl_2: **The past only.** An exception rereads what happened. For the future, close the date in the calendar or adjust the price: removing a still-sellable day from the reference would create two truths for the same night — its revenue in the actuals, its nights outside the normal.
yfs.exc_expl_3: **These nights stay in the actuals.** A closure for works belongs to what happened; it is only set aside from what is “normal”.
yfs.exc_expl_4: **Without them, the engine gets it wrong in a predictable way.** A month of works at zero nights makes it believe demand collapses in that season — and it will suggest discounting next year.
yfs.legende_personnes: Occupancy in people is not shown on this screen, but these limits concern it and will apply to price suggestions.
yfs.legende_estimee: {n} period(s) with **estimated capacity**: before the calendar went live, a past day with no trace is deemed open, unless an exception is declared. Occupancy rate and RevPAR there are estimates, not measurements.

cp.voix: Each host counts as one vote, even with several listings. Your “below”, “equivalent” and “better” answers shift this price by at most a quarter of the gap between the cheapest and the dearest of your comparables.
cp.d_sous: Computed from the prices your comparables show over the next 6 months. Your usual weekday price is that of your hosts at your strategy’s rank, shifted by your “below” or “better” answers; in each cell, it follows the median gap, between that cell and their own usual price, of those of your hosts who change their prices with the seasons (or, if too few, that of your town’s market), without leaving the cell’s range. Nothing is applied to your prices yet.

mt.avertir: **A market estimate from AirROI’s model, not a price.** This page tells you, day by day, whether the market in your town is rather low, moderate, favourable or at a peak, based on AirROI’s pricing model alone — without your sales history. It shows no price, pushes none, and **controls nothing**: your prices and your calendar do not change.

serrures.aide_titre: How do I get my Seam API key?
serrures.aide_2: Connect your locks (Igloo Home, Nuki, Yale…)
serrures.aide_4: Create a key and copy it (it starts with `seam_`)
serrures.aide_supportees: **Supported locks:** Igloo Home, Nuki, Yale, August, Schlage, Tedee and many more through Seam.
serrures.mode_offline: **Offline mode** — no bridge or hub. Access codes are computed by the lock from an internal algorithm. They are **immutable**: once created, they can be neither changed nor deleted. They expire automatically at their end date. No remote unlock and no access logs.
serrures.mode_connecte: **Connected mode (with bridge)** — adding an IglooHome Bridge unlocks dynamic management: codes revocable at any time, remote unlock from the app, real-time access logs, live lock status. A bridge costs about €80-100 and connects to your Wi-Fi.
serrures.vide_texte: Link your locks (Nuki, Yale, Igloo, August…) to generate and send an access code automatically for every booking. This module is optional: HôteSmart works perfectly well without it.
serrures.info_offline: Access codes generated here can no longer be changed or deleted. They expire automatically at their end date.
serrures.info_connecte: Codes can be revoked at any time and the lock can be unlocked remotely.

cnx.beds24_1: Log in to Beds24 and go to [Settings → Marketplace → API](beds24)
cnx.beds24_2: Click **Generate invite code**. Tick **READ + WRITE** on `bookings` and `properties`. Select **All properties**.
cnx.beds24_3: Copy the generated invite code and paste it below. **Careful: the invite code can only be used once.**
cnx.beds24_4: Click **Connect** — HôteSmart fetches and saves the token automatically.
cnx.invite_exemple: Paste your Beds24 invite code here…
cnx.beds24_note: The Beds24 token expires after **24h**. HôteSmart renews it automatically with the refresh token. If the connection fails, generate a new invite code.
cnx.refresh_ok: Refresh token available — automatic renewal active
cnx.refresh_absent: No refresh token — reconnect with an invite code to enable automatic renewal
cnx.brevo_contexte: One key, two uses. **Text messages** are optional and billed to **your own Brevo account** (~€0.06 per message), not by HôteSmart. **E-mails to the guests** of your direct bookings are also sent from your account, under your name.
cnx.brevo_2: In **My account → API keys** ([direct link](cles)), create a key (it starts with `xkeysib-`).
cnx.brevo_4: Paste the key below and save.
cnx.expediteur_aide: Your guests will see this address as the sender, and their replies will come straight back to it. Only senders **verified** in your Brevo account can be used — [manage my senders](expediteurs).
cnx.circuit_1: Your messages leave from your address, but replies come back to **the HôteSmart inbox**, in the booking's conversation — and not to your mailbox. That keeps the whole conversation in one place, where the assistant can read it.
cnx.circuit_2: You still receive **a copy by e-mail** of each reply, marked as such. Do not reply to it directly: your guest would not see it. Reply from the inbox.
cnx.sender_muet: Brevo did not answer ({erreur}). Try again in a moment.
cnx.sender_aucun_aide: Your Brevo account has no verified sender. Add one at Brevo, then come back: without it, no e-mail can be sent.
cnx.sender_invalide: The saved address (**{email}**) is no longer a verified sender in your Brevo account: **your e-mails to guests are no longer sent**. Choose one above and save.
cnx.ota_texte: Connect your Booking.com, Airbnb and other platform listings directly to your HôteSmart properties. Bookings come in automatically and your calendar stays in sync in real time.
